title: perf-bench-scratch-evelyn-cho-2026-03-23
content:
Quick scratchpad for recent latency/throughput runs. Goal: compare batching+KV cache behavior across A100 vs H100 for redwood-7b-v1 under mixed sequence distributions.

Context / goal:
- Reproduce customer-like workload: 70% short (<=64 tokens), 25% medium (512 tokens), 5% long (2048 tokens).
- Measure tokens/sec and p50/p95 generation latency for different batch sizes and with/without KV caching.
- Hardware: NGC images, single-GPU runs (A100 80GB, H100 80GB).
- Model: redwood-7b-v1 (fp16 runtime path), KV cache enabled in runtime.

Test harness:
- runner: perf/run_inference_bench.py (args below)
- warmup: 30s, steady-state: 120s, concurrency steady ramp (3s)
- metrics: tokens/s, p50/p95 latency per request, CPU load, GPU utilization (nvidia-smi sampling)
- command (example):
  python perf/run_inference_bench.py --model redwood-7b-v1 --gpu A100 --batch 8 --seq-dist mixed-70-25-5 --duration 150 --kv-cache on --workers 6

Raw results (steady-state averages):

A100 (fp16) - KV cache OFF:
config,batch,seq, tokens_per_sec,p50_ms,p95_ms,note
base,1,mix, 7200, 45, 210, cold path per-request
batched,4,mix, 18000, 60, 420, batching overhead + higher p95
batched,8,mix, 26000, 85, 650, p95 suffering on long tails
batched,16,mix, 29000, 130, 1200, saturation + queuing

A100 (fp16) - KV cache ON (prefix reuse for short/medium):
config,batch,seq, tokens_per_sec,p50_ms,p95_ms,note
base-kv,1,mix, 9200, 35, 180, KV speeds up small seqs
batched-kv,4,mix, 24500,48,300, much better p95 improvement
batched-kv,8,mix, 34000, 65, 480, good throughput
batched-kv,16,mix, 36500,100,850, still some tail latency

H100 (fp16) - KV cache OFF:
config,batch,seq, tokens_per_sec,p50_ms,p95_ms,note
base-h,1,mix, 9500, 38, 190, single-threaded improvements on H100
batched-h,4,mix, 25000, 55, 380, similar scaling to A100 but higher throughput
batched-h,8,mix, 36000, 78, 600, good
batched-h,16,mix, 41000, 120, 1000, GPU saturation observed

H100 - KV cache ON:
config,batch,seq, tokens_per_sec,p50_ms,p95_ms,note
h-kv,1,mix, 11800, 28, 150, KV biggest wins on short seqs
h-kv,4,mix, 31000, 42, 260, very stable p95
h-kv,8,mix, 43500, 60, 430, excellent tokens/s
h-kv,16,mix, 48000, 95, 780, throughput tops out

Observations / quick analysis:
- KV cache consistently improves tokens/sec and reduces tail latency, especially for workloads with high prefix reuse (short/medium seqs).
- H100 gives ~1.2-1.3x raw throughput vs A100 in comparable configs; larger batches widen the gap slightly.
- p95 tail is the main problem at higher batch sizes (>=8) due to queuing and stragglers from long sequences.
- Batch=8 with KV on is the best sweet spot for mixed workloads on H100 (throughput high while p95 tolerable).
- Batch=4 is safer if tight p95 SLOs (<=300ms) are required.

Micro-notes on infra and experiments:
- Observed noisy CPU-side serialization when workers > 8 on single GPU; suspect Python GIL and queue contention in runner. Need to try uvloop/process pool offload.
- Batching gains diminish past 16 due to KV cache memory pressure and kernel scheduling.
- Need to record per-request size histograms (we sampled at 10s; want 1s resolution next run).

Next runs / TODOs:
- Repeat H100 batch=8 with 1s resolution histograms and per-token latency breakdown (kernel vs memcpy).
- Try mixed-precision path with int8 quantization profile q4f16 to check throughput/cost tradeoffs (possible quality regression; sample on eval set).
- Run multi-GPU pipelined test (2x H100) to validate sharding + batch packing at scale.
- File an infra ticket for runner rewrite: RED-1509 (reduce Python-side contention).

Notes for Sam/Noah:
- Sharing raw logs at: s3://redwood-perf/logs/evelyn/2026-03-23/ (large tarball)
- PR with minor runtime tweak is up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789 (contains batching scheduler tweak)
- Linear: RED-1423 is the ongoing scheduling story; correlate with our findings

Conclusions (informal):
- For PLG hosted tier, default to batch=4 w/ KV on for cost/latency balance on A100.
- For Dedicated/Higher-tier compute on H100, offer batch=8 w/ KV as default and a performance SKU for batch=16 if throughput > cost priority.

Random scratch thoughts:
- Could we expose dynamic batch sizing per-route based on observed seq distribution? Might auto-tune batch target around observed p95.
- Consider lightweight C-extension for runner enqueue path to remove Python GIL on hot path.
